title: Detection of Smooth Muscle Actin-Alpha and Measurement of Oxidative Damage in Neonatal Mouse Intestine
author: Hu, Sevier, et al.
materials: Anti-Actin, α-Smooth Muscle (1:400 dilution for western blotting)
Anti-Actin, α-Smooth Muscle-FITC (1:100 dilution for whole mount immunofluorescent stain)
Rabbit Anti-Mouse IgG H&L (HRP)(1:2000 dilution western blotting)
Halt™ Protease and Phosphatase Inhibitor Cocktail

This step labels protein carbonyl with biotin-hydrazide.16.Take 100–200 μg of protein samples from each tube, top to 400 μL with homogenization buffer with protease inhibitor from step 12.17.Add 10 μL of EZ-link Hydrazide-biotin (stock solution: 50 mM in DMSO, store at −20°C) to the sample, bringing the total volume of labeling mix to 410 μL.18.Incubate the labeling mix at 20°C–25°C with gentle agitation for 2 h.19.Concentrate sample and remove unreacted Hydrazide-biotin and SDS.a.Add samples (410 μL) to an Amicon Ultra-0.5 mL centrifugal filter, prepped following manufacturer’s instructions.b.Spin at 14,000 g for 10 min.c.Discard flowthrough, add 400 μL PBS, then spin at 14,000 g for 10 min. Repeat twice.d.Recover the samples into a clean tube by spinning at 1,000 g for 2 min. The volume of concentrated samples should be around 40 μL. Add another 20 μL PBS to bring sample volume to 60 μL. Measure protein concentration again.Alternatives: We use Amicon Ultra 0.5 mL DNA/Protein centrifugal filters, UFC501024, Millipore for step 19. Other protein desalting and concentrating columns or methods such as TCA precipitation should be equally effective.Note: Concentrated samples should be arranged into three aliquots for streptavidin pulldown assay, αSMA immunoprecipitation (IP), and lysate control. We recommend using roughly 45% of the protein samples for Streptavidin pulldown, 45% for αSMA IP assay, and 10% for the lysate control (step 31).

steps.title: Standard intestine isolation
steps.instruction: Euthanize pregnant dam (if embryonic) then decapitate embryos or neonates, pin paws ventral side up on a Styrofoam tray, cut open skin and peritoneum, optionally open rib cage and remove visceral organs, lift organs with fine forceps while cutting dorsal connective tissue with spring scissors, place intestine in ice‑cold PBS, insert spring scissors at duodenal end and gently snip along length to expose interior, shake intestine in ice‑cold PBS several times to remove contents, then proceed to fixation (step 3) or flash‑freeze (step 4) as desired.

substeps.instruction: a. Follow institutional IACUC protocol for dam euthanasia.
b. Decapitate embryos/neonates before gut isolation.
c. Pin mouse paws ventral side up on Styrofoam dissection tray.
d. Open skin/peritoneum to expose intestine; optionally open rib cage in very young mice.
e. Use fine forceps and spring scissors to detach dorsal connective tissue.
f. Transfer intestine to ice‑cold PBS.
g. Insert spring scissors at duodenal end, snip longitudinally to open tube.
h. Shake intestine in ice‑cold PBS several times to clear luminal contents.

steps.title: Alternative perfusion dissection
steps.instruction: Euthanize embryos or neonates by hypothermia on ice for 7–10 min, pin paws ventral side up, create a minimal wound at lower rib cage edge to expose heart apex, slowly inject 10 mL ice‑cold PBS into left ventricle using a 31 G × ½″ needle, observe pale lungs/liver/mesentery indicating successful perfusion, then continue with step 1c of the standard isolation.

substeps.instruction: a. Keep mouse on weighing boat on ice for 7–10 min until no movement.
b. Pin paws ventral side up on Styrofoam tray.
c. Make a small wound at lower rib cage to expose heart apex.
d. Inject 10 mL ice‑cold PBS into left ventricle with 31 G × ½″ needle; organs should turn pale.
e. Proceed to step 1c (pinning) of the standard isolation.

steps.title: Methanol fixation for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Place dissected intestine in ice‑cold 100 % methanol, gently agitate to flatten, change to fresh ice‑cold methanol every 5 min for 2–3 times until solution is colorless, then store tissue in fresh ice‑cold methanol at –20 °C (up to three months).

substeps.instruction: a. Add tissue to ice‑cold 100 % methanol, agitate gently; bile pigments dissolve.
b. Replace methanol with fresh ice‑cold methanol every 5 min, repeat 2–3 times until clear.
c. Store tissue in fresh ice‑cold methanol at –20 °C; pause point up to three months.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze tissue for carbonyl assay
steps.instruction: Immediately flash‑freeze intestine in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C (up to three months). Collect a piece of tissue (e.g., tail or limb) for genotyping before freezing if needed.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue for protein extraction
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen intestine samples, thaw on ice 5–10 min, prepare homogenization buffer with phosphatase/protease inhibitor cocktail, add 500 mL buffer per intestine (adjust for larger tissue), grind with a tissue pestle until no visible chunks remain, then shear genomic DNA by passing homogenate through a 1 mL syringe with a <25 G needle 30 times on ice.

substeps.instruction: a. Thaw samples on ice 5–10 min.
b. Make homogenization buffer by adding inhibitor cocktail to Biotin‑Hydrazide buffer; add 500 mL per intestine.
c. Homogenize with pestle until homogeneous.
d. Shear DNA: pass through 1 mL syringe with <25 G needle 30 times on ice.

steps.title: Low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin homogenate at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C, then collect supernatant into a new tube.

steps.title: Add SDS to 2 % final
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 % SDS stock in homogenization buffer with protease inhibitor, then add 1 : 10 (v/v) of this stock to the collected supernatant to reach a final SDS concentration of 2 %.

steps.title: Heat sample
steps.instruction: Incubate the SDS‑containing sample at 65 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the heated sample at 18,000 g for 1 h at 4 °C and collect the supernatant into a fresh tube.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of the supernatant, using an assay compatible with 2 % SDS or measuring before SDS addition and adjusting calculations accordingly; include a buffer‑only control.

steps.title: Biotin‑hydrazide labeling of carbonyls
steps.instruction: Take 100–200 µg of protein, bring volume to 400 µL with homogenization buffer containing protease inhibitor, add 10 µL EZ‑link Hydrazide‑biotin (50 mM in DMSO, stored at –20 °C) to reach a total volume of 410 µL, incubate at 20–25 °C with gentle agitation for 2 h.

substeps.instruction: a. Adjust protein to 400 µL buffer.
b. Add 10 µL 50 mM EZ‑link Hydrazide‑biotin.
c. Incubate 20–25 °C, gentle agitation, 2 h.

steps.title: Concentrate and desalt labeled proteins
steps.instruction: Load the 410 µL labeling mix onto an Amicon Ultra 0.5 mL centrifugal filter (UFC501024, Millipore), spin at 14,000 g for 10 min, discard flow‑through, add 400 µL PBS and spin again (repeat twice), then recover concentrate by spinning at 1,000 g for 2 min; final concentrate (~40 µL) is brought to 60 µL with 20 µL PBS and protein concentration re‑measured. Aliquot roughly 45 % for streptavidin pulldown, 45 % for αSMA immunoprecipitation, and 10 % as lysate control.

substeps.instruction: a. Transfer 410 µL to Amicon Ultra 0.5 mL filter.
b. Spin 14,000 g, 10 min; discard flow‑through.
c. Add 400 µL PBS, spin 14,000 g, 10 min; repeat twice.
d. Recover concentrate at 1,000 g, 2 min (≈40 µL).
e. Add 20 µL PBS to reach 60 µL total; re‑measure protein.
f. Divide into ~45 % streptavidin pulldown, ~45 % αSMA IP, ~10 % lysate control.
